primitives.name: Stimulus-Object Behavioral Mapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: For the purposes of a behavioral psychology the stimulus-object, as physics describes it, becomes thus the "source" of the discriminanda- manipulanda- and the means-end-supports, which the given organism in some concrete sensory motor situation or set of situations expects and finds—or perhaps fails to find.
primitives.assumptions: Organism's behavioral repertoire is finite and deterministic within sensory-motor constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S exceeds O's capacity for discriminanda-manipulanda resolution.

layer2.mapping: The stimulus-object in physics becomes the behavioral source for organismic response prediction in GSE; GSI models this via conditional probability P(R|S,O).

primitives.name: Knowledge Conditional Behavioral Needs
primitives.verbatim_quote: For we are asserting that all human knowledge, including physics, purposive behaviorism and our own present remarks, are but a resultant of, and limited by, human behavioral needs and human behavioral capacities.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'K': 'Knowledge representation (dimensionless)', 'B_N': 'Behavioral needs (vector of categorical/ordinal units)', 'B_C': 'Behavioral capacities (vector of scalar units)'}
primitives.assumptions: Knowledge is a product of organismic behavioral constraints and needs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When B_N or B_C are misaligned with K's structure.

layer2.mapping: GSI encodes K as a function of B_N and B_C; GSE uses this kernel to constrain state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy of knowledge representation under behavioral constraint

primitives.name: Behavioral Map Truth Criterion
primitives.verbatim_quote: That "map" knowledge is "true" which "works," given the particular behavior-needs and the particular behaviorcapacities of the type of organism gathering such knowledge.
primitives.assumptions: Truth is defined operationally by functional utility within organismic context.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When W fails to correlate with B_N and B_C.

layer2.mapping: GSI evaluates T = f(W, B_N, B_C); GSE applies T to validate situational mappings.
layer2.telemetry: Functional consistency of knowledge against behavioral outcomes

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that all knowledge—whether physical or psychological—is shaped by the organism’s behavioral needs and capacities. The first primitive, 'Stimulus-Object Behavioral Mapping', formalizes how external stimuli become meaningful through the lens of sensorimotor expectations. It establishes a foundational link between physical description and behavioral interpretation. The second, 'Knowledge Conditional Behavioral Needs', asserts that knowledge itself is not neutral but emerges from the interaction between organismic needs and capabilities. This leads to the third primitive, 'Behavioral Map Truth Criterion', which defines truth not as absolute correspondence but as operational success within a behavioral framework. These primitives form a triadic system where the physical world is interpreted through behavioral lenses, and truth is validated by its functional efficacy. The failure mode occurs when these mappings break down due to mismatched behavioral assumptions or insufficient capacity to process stimuli.
